question.problem:
The matrix $V$ is given below. Let ${v}_{1}$, ${v}_{2}$,  ${v}_{3}$ and ${v}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $V.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{v}_{1},{v}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(V).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${v}_{2}={x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}.$ 

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 10 & 20 & 10 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$,  $\mathbf{a}_3$, and $\mathbf{a}_4$ be the respective columns of $A.$ Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/7ac785c65d422703ca7fb6aec74a01ca2c810d19a5e04c6ab69e8bac5474a208.svg) is a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A).$ If that is the case, find $x_1 \cdot x_2$, where $\mathbf{a}_4=x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/e51162b4ff66539ceaa052770e4130e9abbca4d3375e958b300b6b5750ada522.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & -14 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & -14 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & -12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ that is to say,
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/4ee85100c48c5cee019651a91a225f4226cc3dbe8f58a31053f90b6c3bb78ff6.svg)

Now, since the $4$th column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{a}_4$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128538/assets/001938c7fd2e2c54de92c071cca5551a93d13a8efe75bd2895aed4cb2bcd7256.svg)

This gives us $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 2 \cdot (-3) = -6.$
